summary: Abolished the Akron land district in Colorado and transferred its business to the Sterling land district.
Created the Wenaha Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands straddling Oregon and Washington, reserving the area from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Set apart the Leadville Forest Reserve in Colorado as a public reservation, covering public lands described as partly timbered and excepting lands already lawfully claimed.
Established the Sevier Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Utah and closed it to settlement, apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Reserved partly timbered public lands in northeastern Oregon as the Chesnimnus Forest Reserve, withdrawing them from settlement except for existing lawful claims.
Created the Elkhorn Forest Reserve in Montana, setting aside partly timbered public lands as a public reservation closed to settlement, apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Established the Gunnison Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Colorado, reserving them from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

Combined the Pikes Peak Timber Land Reserve, the Plum Creek Timber Land Reserve and the South Platte Forest Reserve, plus added lands, into a single Pikes Peak Forest Reserve in Colorado, superseding the earlier proclamations.
Amended Schedule A of the civil service rules so that one law officer in the War Department's Bureau of Insular Affairs could be hired without examination.
Allowed a carriage driver for the Secretary of the Treasury to be appointed without a civil-service examination.
Put the administration of aids to navigation under the Department of Commerce and Labor.
Restored to the public domain two sections of land in southern California once reserved for the Capitan Grande band of Mission Indians but left out of the band's later selection and patent.

Suspended foreign discriminating tonnage duties and imposts on Panamanian vessels and their cargoes, after Panama showed it levied no such duties on American ships, for as long as that reciprocal treatment continues.
Allowed John Ball Osborne to be appointed chief of the State Department's Bureau of Trade Relations without regard to civil service rules.
Canceled Executive Order 302-A of March 10, 1905, and reserved other lands in its place.
Enlarged the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve by adding partly timbered lands in Colorado, redrawing the boundaries of a reserve first created in Wyoming.
Amended Executive Order 310-C to leave out the lands making up Louis Zeph's homestead entry.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve seven tracts of land in the Philippine Islands for military purposes.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve nine more tracts of land in Jolo, Philippine Islands, for military purposes.
Approved a War Secretary recommendation to amend a June 1904 order, changing the borders of the military reservation at Zamboanga on Mindanao in the Philippines.
Allowed Chauncey O. Howard of the Bureau of Pensions to move from an excepted to a non-excepted position without regard to civil service rules.
Ordered that every government contract include a clause forbidding the use of convict labor.

Let a superintendent, chief chemist and first assistant chemist at the Washington filtration plant be hired outside civil service rules, since the plant was expected to pass to the District of Columbia's municipal service within a year.
Allowed Mrs. Eleanor Relyea to be reinstated in the departmental service without reference to civil service rules.
Redrew the boundaries of the Bitter Root Forest Reserve in Idaho and Montana, releasing some lands, including lands in Idaho, and adding other partly timbered lands.
Added partly timbered public lands in Idaho to the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, which had covered lands in Wyoming and Montana.
Allowed William J. Humphreys to be appointed professor of meteorological physics in the Weather Bureau without examination.
Set aside the Henrys Lake Forest Reserve in Idaho on partly timbered public lands, closing it to settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Changed the boundaries of the Uintah land district in Utah, issued in the form of a proclamation.
Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve 13 described tracts in Alaska for the Army Signal Corps.
Created the Weiser Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.
Established the Sawtooth Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Idaho and withdrew it from settlement, apart from existing lawful claims.

Designated the entire Wichita Forest Reserve in Oklahoma Territory as a game preserve and breeding place for game animals and birds, making hunting or trapping there unlawful except under Agriculture Department regulations.
Reserved partly timbered public lands in northern California as the Lassen Peak Forest Reserve, closed to settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.
Created the Maury Mountain Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon, withdrawing the area from settlement apart from existing lawful claims.
Set the pay for enlisted men of the Navy detailed to serve as ship's tailors.
Set aside the Payette Forest Reserve in Idaho on partly timbered public lands, reserved from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.
Established the San Juan Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in southwestern Colorado, excepting lands already lawfully claimed.
Allowed Albert C. Muhse to be appointed a special agent of the Bureau of Corporations, at $2,000 a year, without a civil-service examination.
Redrew the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve in Colorado, releasing some lands back to the public domain and adding other partly timbered lands.
Allowed five employees in the Isthmian Canal service to be appointed without regard to civil service rules.
Created the Park Range Forest Reserve in Colorado, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Enlarged the San Isabel Forest Reserve in Colorado, first proclaimed in 1902, to take in additional partly timbered public lands.
Redrew the boundaries of the Washington Forest Reserve, releasing some lands and adding other partly timbered lands in the state of Washington.
Set apart the Wet Mountains Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Colorado, closed to settlement except for existing lawful claims.
Established the Cassia Forest Reserve in southern Idaho, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve Grass Island in Grays Harbor, Washington, for military purposes.
Amended the Executive Order of March 26, 1901, which set the limits of punishment for enlisted men of the Army.
Created the Cochetopah Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Colorado, reserving them from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.
Reserved partly timbered public lands in southwestern Colorado as the Montezuma Forest Reserve, closed to settlement apart from existing lawful claims.
Allowed C. H. Chapman, a Civil War veteran, to be appointed a copyist in the General Land Office without regard to civil service rules, in view of his earlier service in the Census Office.

Amended civil service Rule XI so classified Indian Service employees could be promoted without examination to superintendent of an Indian school, on the Commissioner of Indian Affairs' statement of their qualifications.

Freed the hiring of skilled and unskilled laborers at naval hospitals from civil service rules and navy-yard regulations, citing hours, varied duties and pay arrangements that made those rules impracticable.

Amended Schedule A of the civil service rules to except mechanics, skilled tradesmen and laborers on field construction or repair work who, in the Commission's view, could not be appointed from registers of eligibles.
Established the Uncompahgre Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in western Colorado, withdrawn from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.
Allowed Mary T. Waggaman to be appointed a clerk in the Bureau of Labor without regard to civil service rules.
Named a Board of Consulting Engineers to consider plans for the canal across the Isthmus of Panama.
Allowed James W. Plake, an Indian, to be permanently appointed a copyist in the Office of Indian Affairs.
Extended U.S. copyright benefits to subjects of Norway, after official assurances that Norwegian law gave Americans copyright on substantially the same basis as its own citizens.

Announced the death of Secretary of State John Hay and ordered flags at half-mast for ten days at U.S. embassies, legations, forts, naval stations and vessels, with executive departments in Washington closed on the day of his funeral.
Allowed Charles W. Bell to be appointed finance clerk in the Post-Office Department without regard to civil service rules.
Placed the aids to navigation for Tutuila and the other American Samoan islands under the Department of Commerce and Labor.
Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve lands at Seward, Alaska, for military telegraph purposes.
Forbade officers of the Army and Navy from using outside influence to win appointments, transfers, promotions and similar favors.
Allowed Abram B. Frisbie to be permanently appointed a watchman in the Interior Department, at the Secretary's discretion, without a civil-service examination.
Amended the regulations for hiring unskilled laborers in federal offices outside Washington, D.C.
Allowed Frank B. McCown to be reinstated as a clerk in the Quartermaster's Department at large, at the Secretary of War's request.
Extended Allen Hazen's employment as an engineer at the Washington filtration plant for seven more months.
Moved certain lands out of the Uintah Indian Reservation and into the Uintah Forest Reserve in Utah, redrawing the forest reserve's boundaries.

Opened the unallotted lands of the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah to settlement and entry under the homestead and townsite laws beginning August 28, 1905, setting out how applicants would register and apply.
Created the Diamond Mountain Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in California, reserving it from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation to remove 28 acres from the Fort Bayard Military Reservation in New Mexico that had been mistakenly included in a private patent.
Gave James L. Bristow, special Panama Railroad commissioner, more time and pay to finish his report.
Changed the boundaries of the Fort Gibbon Military Reservation in Alaska.
Moved the office of the Gila land district in Arizona from Tucson to Phoenix.
Allowed Henry Summers to be appointed a clerk in the New York pension agency without a civil-service examination.
Enlarged the Gila River Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, first proclaimed in 1899, to take in more partly timbered public lands, and gave it a new name: the Gila Forest Reserve.
Further enlarged the Payson Forest Reserve in Utah, adding partly timbered lands and redrawing its boundaries.

Approved the Acting Interior Secretary's recommendation to add certain Utah lands to the Uintah Indian Reservation despite an earlier application by the State of Utah for water rights from Rock Creek.
Allowed Gertrude Weaver to be permanently appointed a clerk in the Signal Service without examination.
Approved the Acting Interior Secretary's recommendation concerning additional lands within Utah's Uintah Indian Reservation, aimed at protecting the Indians' water rights.
Set aside the Short Pine Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in South Dakota, closed to settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.
Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation on how to dispose of the Fort Shaw Indian School Reservation in Montana.
Created the Garden City Forest Reserve in western Kansas, reserving public lands from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.
Added partly timbered California lands to the Sierra Forest Reserve, using boundary authority Congress extended earlier in 1905 when it moved lands out of Yosemite National Park and into the reserve.
Reserved described lands on Revillagigedo Island, Alaska, as the site for a lighthouse depot.
Allowed Charles W. Spicer to be employed in the Bureau of the Census without examination.
Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation to declare lands conveyed from the Port Madison Indian Reservation a military reservation.
Reserved described lands in New Mexico for the Pueblo Indians of Santa Clara.
Reserved tracts in the Uintah Indian Reservation lands of Utah, chosen by the Uintah Allotment Commission and approved by the Interior Department, as sites for future townsites.
Abolished the Ashland and Eau Claire land districts in Wisconsin and transferred their business to the Wausau land district.
Allowed Thomas Harper to be appointed a clerk in the Quartermaster's Department at large without examination.

Changed the schedule for the Uintah Indian Reservation land opening so applicants holding drawing numbers 1 to 111, rather than 1 to 50, would be heard each day at the Vernal, Utah, land office starting August 28, 1905.
Withdrew certain Uintah Indian Reservation lands in Utah from disposal before the opening, as a reservoir site to conserve the Indians' water supply or for general agricultural development.
Extended the deadline for the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to finish its work to March 2, 1906.
